items.readme:
# VIctory

Runs Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series X|S) natively on Windows, from files
the user supplies.

The title's x86-64 code runs unchanged inside our process; VIctory supplies
the platform underneath it and converts the title's data, ahead of time where
it can and on first use where it must (shaders). See
[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Status (2026-11-23)

**Not playable yet.** The title boots, runs its menus at its own 30 fps and
loads the world, where rendering fails.

| Stage | State |
|-------|-------|
| Boot, first-boot screens (accessibility, language, settings, legal) | works, 30 fps |
| Intro video with sound | works |
| Start screen, profile and saves | works |
| Loading into the world (about 50 s) | works |
| The world (first mission's intro) | reached and runs with indirect draws; its title card renders, the scene after it is still dark; 0.5-1.8 s per frame |

Tested on one machine: Windows 11, AMD RX 6700 XT.

> **Warning.** Entering the world on a real GPU can currently hang it, and
> Windows then resets the display driver (every monitor goes black for a
> moment). To look further, use a diagnostics build with
> `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1`, which renders on the software adapter.

What each part does today and what it still needs:

| Subsystem | Today | Needs |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Loader | Runs the title's executable and its DLLs in our process; crash reports name the faulting code and are kept in `crashes.log` | – |
| Runtime services | One signed-in offline user, licences, packages, saves that survive a kill at any step, text entry dialog | Speech is silent; the dialog and relaunch are untested live |
| Network | Offline by design: the title cannot reach the network | – |
| Files and streaming | Archives and streamed data read, zlib and BCPack decoded in parallel | Loading is limited by writes into title memory |
| Input | XInput pads, keyboard, keyboard stand-in pad | Trigger rumble |
| Audio | Menu, video and loading sound; XMA voices and Opus streams decode | Reverb is silent; Opus results unverified against the title |
| GPU: menus | Draws, compute and presentation on host D3D12; only changed title memory is copied | Frame pacing drifts on one screen in release builds |
| GPU: world | Mesh pipelines, shader-written buffers, descriptor lifetimes, indirect execution (arguments clamped), pipelines made by worker threads and kept on disk | Most of the scene is still missing (untranslated shaders drop draws); frames take seconds; real queries, depth bounds, HDR and scaling are missing |
| Shaders | Console GPU code recompiled to DXIL at first use, cached on disk. Menus: all. World: mesh 8,191 of 8,506, vertex/pixel 10,617 of 12,346, compute 1,643 of 2,539 | 64-bit image atomics, merged geometry stages, the ray-tracing builder's shaders; some compute programs need a GPU with 64-lane waves |
| Textures | Console tiled layouts and detiling for the modes the title uses | Render-target metadata planes |
| Series S mode | Runs through the menus to the loading screen | The world, as above |

## Getting started

Requirements: Windows 10/11 x64, a CPU with AVX2, a Direct3D 12 GPU with
shader model 6.6 (and mesh shaders for the world), Rust (pinned in
`rust-toolchain.toml`).

The title also needs several GiB of available Windows commit at startup.
Check **Committed** under **Task Manager → Performance → Memory**. If
`crashes.log` reports Windows error 1455, close other applications or increase
the Windows paging file size, then retry.

```powershell
cargo xtask install-hooks                # asset-policy check on every commit
copy victory.example.toml victory.toml   # then set your paths (outside the repo)
cargo test --workspace                   # needs no game data
cargo run -p victory -- config           # check your paths
```

Run the title:

```powershell
cargo build --release -p victory
target\release\victory.exe run <game dir>\<the title's exe> --execute
```

The window caption shows the framerate. Saves, settings and `crashes.log`
are kept under the data folder (default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\victory\data`), derived
data under the cache folder.

Input: XInput pads. With none connected the keyboard is a pad while the
title's window has focus:

| Keys | Pad |
|------|-----|
| W A S D / I J K L | left / right stick |
| arrows | D-pad |
| Enter, Backspace, X, Y | A, B, X, Y |
| Q / E, Z / C | shoulders, triggers |
| F / H | stick clicks |
| Esc, Tab | Menu, View |

## Commands

```
victory inspect <exe|dll> [--imports] [--exports]
victory census [paths...] [--missing] [--strict]
victory lib-exports <import.lib> [--list]
victory shader-info [paths...] [--verbose] [--disasm]
victory translate [paths...] [--validate] [--pipelines] [--list] [--jobs N]
victory run <exe> [--execute] [--unimplemented trap|zero] [--strict]
            [--console series-x|series-s] [-- <title arguments>]
victory config
```

Logging: `VICTORY_LOG=victory_loader=trace,info` (a release build logs
info and above).

## Debugging

A release build has no debugging aids. Build them in with

```powershell
cargo build --profile diag -p victory --features diagnostics   # target\diag\victory.exe
```

| Variable | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `VICTORY_LOG=<target>=debug,...` | debug and trace output |
| `VICTORY_STACKS=20,60` | every thread's stack at those seconds |
| `VICTORY_WATCH=<rva>,...` | logs a title u32 when it changes |
| `VICTORY_KEYS=30:Enter,35:X` | presses keys at those seconds, focus or not |
| `VICTORY_CRASH_SAVE=<rva>:<len>,...` | saves title memory to the cache folder on a crash |
| `VICTORY_CAPTURE=<dir>` | saves presented frames (powers of two, or `VICTORY_CAPTURE_FRAMES=<list>`) |
| `VICTORY_DUMP_TARGETS=1` | with the two above, saves every render target of those frames |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_DEBUG=1` | host debug layer |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_GBV=1` | with the above, GPU-based validation (bad descriptor use reported, not faulted; slow) |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_DRED=1` | on a GPU failure, the allocation hit and the commands in flight |
| `VICTORY_SKIP_PIPELINES=<hash>,...` | omit draws and dispatches, including indirect ones, whose pipeline contains a listed 16-digit shader hash |
| `VICTORY_GPU_TIMING=1` | with the above, each list of a submission run and timed on its own; slow lists logged with their slowest commands |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1` | host device on the software adapter (slow; cannot reset the driver) |
| `VICTORY_SHADER_LOOP_LIMIT=<n>` | translated shader loops stop after `n` iterations per lane instead of 2^20 (own shader cache entries); if a lower `n` makes world frames much faster, loops hitting the limit are what makes them slow |
| `VICTORY_AUDIO_CAPTURE=<file.wav>` | records what the title plays (our process only) |
| `VICTORY_XMA_DUMP=<dir>` | saves the first 32 XMA voices' context and input |

Every build appends crashes and host GPU failures to `crashes.log` in the
title's data folder.

## License

GPL-3.0-or-later. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

items.readme:
# PortWatch VI

**Does GTA VI run on PC yet?** A static GitHub Pages site that tracks every serious community effort to recompile, emulate or port the leaked Xbox Series build of GTA VI to PC. All efforts are scored on one ladder, and a scout refreshes the data every 3 hours.

- One headline progress bar shows the closest effort, with the top projects pinned to it.
- A live countdown runs to the missing executable's expected drop.
- A leaderboard card per effort shows its own bar, milestone ladder, groundwork breakdown, what works and what's blocking.
- Further sections cover the watchlist of early projects, a toolkit of asset tools, the scout's inbox of new candidates, and fake-download warnings.

No game files, keys or executables are hosted or linked, ever.

## Deploy on GitHub Pages

1. Create a new GitHub repository and push this folder to its `main` branch.
2. In the repo, open **Settings → Pages** and set **Source** to **GitHub Actions**.
3. Open **Settings → Actions → General** and make sure workflows are allowed.
4. Open **Actions → Scout → Run workflow** to run the first scout. It commits fresh data and deploys the site.

Each deploy also runs `scripts/build-site.mjs`, which turns `data/tracker.json` into pages search engines can read: one page per news story (`news/<id>.html`), a news archive, an RSS feed (`news/feed.xml`) and `sitemap.xml`. It then pings [IndexNow](https://www.indexnow.org/) (Bing, Yandex and others; no account needed) with the URLs that changed since the last deploy. For Google, add the site in Search Console and submit `sitemap.xml`.

From then on, `Scout` runs every 3 hours (00:17, 03:17, 06:17 … UTC) on GitHub's servers, so no computer of yours needs to be on. Any push to `main` redeploys the site through `Deploy site`. To change the frequency, edit the `cron` line in `.github/workflows/scout.yml`. For example, `17 6 * * *` runs it once a day. GitHub can delay scheduled runs by a few minutes when it's busy.

## What the scout does (`scripts/scout.mjs`)

1. **Refreshes** every tracked repo: stars, forks, issues, last push, commits in the last 7 days, and whether it's gone (404, or 451 for a DMCA block). It also hashes each README to notice changes.
2. **Spots claims.** If a README newly says GTA VI boots, reaches the menu or runs at some FPS, the card shows an "unverified claim" banner and the change feed records it.
3. **Discovers** new repos from GitHub and GitLab searches (`scout.queries` in `data/tracker.json`), Hacker News, Bluesky, Mastodon, Lemmy and 4chan, plus Reddit and X when keys are set, by pulling GitHub links out of posts. It also gathers **headlines** from the Google News and Bing News feeds, keeping only stories about the leak, ports, takedowns, scams or official news. And it **watches GitHub's public DMCA log** for new Take-Two or Rockstar notices, flagging any tracked project they name. On 4chan it uses the free read-only API, at one request per second. It opens only /v/ threads that mention GTA VI together with port terms (recomp, emulator, leak, executable, GitHub…), plus /vg/'s /gtag/ and /emugen/ generals. Change the boards with `scout.chan.boards`. Nothing from 4chan is shown on the site except, indirectly, repo names that pass every filter.
4. **Filters out spam** such as clone networks, download lures and "PC installer" repos. Their names are counted under *There is no download*, never linked.
5. **Filters out copies.** Re-uploads of tracked projects are flagged when they reuse a tracked project's name or have a README that is 60% or more identical, renamed copies included. Original fan games and repos without a real README are skipped too. Candidates already waiting are re-checked every run.
6. **Scores substance** from code language, size, technical depth, status tables, tests and commit activity. Repos with real code go to **New candidates**, shown as plain text and not linked until reviewed. Thin or off-topic ones are remembered and skipped.
7. **Writes news** (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). Claude searches the web for takedowns, bans, confirmed leaks, legal news, scams and official announcements, then writes up to two short original articles. It runs at most every 11 hours, not on every 3-hourly scout run, to keep costs down. A source is kept only if it came up in Claude's own search. Each article's image is the source's preview image, credited and linked back; it falls back to a generated cover.
8. **Records** a change feed, the day's leader score for the sparkline, and a run summary.

### Optional secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions)

| Secret | What it enables |
|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | **Claude review.** When a tracked README changes, or a new candidate shows up, Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`) reads the README and recent commits and re-scores the effort. It also promotes or rejects candidates automatically. Guardrails clamp the output: a GTA VI milestone only counts if Claude quotes text that really appears in the repo, and groundwork can rise at most 0.3 per run. Reviews are capped at 12 per run. Each costs very roughly $0.05–0.20, depending on README size. |
| `REDDIT_CLIENT_ID` / `REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET` | Reddit search. Reddit blocks anonymous API and RSS access, so Reddit is skipped without these. The API is free for small non-commercial use, but since late 2025 every new app needs Reddit's manual approval. Create a "script" app at reddit.com/prefs/apps, request access, and paste the client ID and secret here once approved. |
| `X_BEARER_TOKEN` | X recent search. This needs a paid X API tier. |

Without any secrets the scout still runs on every keyless source, and new finds wait in *New candidates* for review.

### Daily Claude editor (alternative to an API key)

Instead of `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, a scheduled Claude session on the maintainer's PC can run once a day, following [EDITOR.md](EDITOR.md). It re-scores changed projects, reviews candidates, verifies leads, keeps the countdown accurate and writes news, then commits `data/tracker.json`. It also reads 4chan's /v/, /vg/ and /g/ in full through `tools/chan-scan.ps1`, which gathers GTA VI port discussion from live threads and the public archives into a local digest (`.chan/`, never committed). The scout only picks GitHub links out of those threads. It uses the maintainer's Claude plan and needs no separate billing. It runs while the Claude desktop app is open; a missed run happens on the next launch.

## Editing the data by hand

Everything lives in `data/tracker.json`:

- `efforts[]`: each effort has a `tier` (`tracked` puts it in the race, `watchlist` lists it below). Each also carries `groundwork` (four 0–1 values), `gta` (`loads`/`boots`/`menu`/`ingame` are 0, 0.5 or 1, plus `fps` and `stability`), and short `highlights` and `blockers`.
- `exe`: drives the countdown. If the release time is announced, set `expectedAt` (ISO time) and `timeAnnounced: true`. When it drops, set `status: "released"` and `releasedAt`, and the countdown turns into a "time since release" clock.
- `candidates[]`: move one into `efforts` to promote it, or into `ignored` to dismiss it.
- `site.heroImage` / `site.heroCredit`: hero artwork (see below).

Scoring is in `assets/js/scoring.js`, shared by the site and the scout. Groundwork fills 0–25%. After that, milestones sit at Exe runs 25, First frame 40, Main menu 55, In-game 70, 30 FPS 85 and Stable 100.

## Hero artwork

The hero shows an original sunset illustration until you add a photo. To use official GTA VI artwork, download a wallpaper or artwork image from Rockstar's official GTA VI site and save it as `assets/img/hero.jpg`, ideally about 2400px wide. The site finds it automatically and shows the credit line from `site.heroCredit`.

## Local preview

Any static server works. On Windows without Node or Python:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/serve.ps1 -Port 8080
```

Then open http://localhost:8080. To try the scout locally with Node 20+, run `node scripts/scout.mjs --dry-run`. Setting `GITHUB_TOKEN` avoids the 60-requests-per-hour anonymous limit.

## Disclaimer

Fan-made and unofficial. Not affiliated with Rockstar Games, Take-Two or Microsoft. Scores are editorial estimates from public READMEs, commits and issues, and self-reported claims are labelled. Maintainers who think their project is mis-scored can open an issue with evidence.

items.description: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow: profile Python, Node or Ruby apps, port the hot functions with your coding agent, prove they behave the same.
items.readme:
Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow.

Rewriting a whole app in Rust costs months, minute-long compiles and gigabytes of `target/`. Most of the runtime sits in a few functions anyway. **fast-anything** finds those functions, has your coding agent port *only them* to Rust, proves the port gives the same results on real recorded calls, and swaps it in. One command, fully reversible.

## Install ```sh npm i -g @el4cteo/fast-anything # or: cargo install fast-anything ``` Ports are compiled with your Rust toolchain ([rustup](https://rustup.rs)). ## Use ```sh fast-anything go --agent claude -- python app.py # or: -- node app.ts / bun app.ts / deno run -A app.ts / ruby app.rb / java App.java / mvn exec:java / gradle run / go run . / php app.php / clang -O2 main.c ``` Or step by step: | command | what it does | |---|---| | `scan -- ` | profiles the app, ranks functions by time × how portable they are | | `port [id]` | records up to 500 real calls, creates a one-function Rust crate + `TASK.md` | | `verify` | release-builds the port and replays every recorded call | | `enable` / `disable` | swaps the Rust in or out (one marked block, removed byte for byte) | | `bench` | times the whole app, original vs Rust, interleaved runs | | `report` | markdown + SVG card for your PR | | `doctor` | checks Rust, your runtimes and your agents | `--agent` takes `claude`, `codex`, or any command that reads a prompt on stdin. Without it, hand `TASK.md` to whatever you use. ## Proof, not vibes

That port looked right but compared bytes instead of characters. 148 of 500 real calls caught it. On top of the recorded calls, fast-anything derives extra cases and lets the original answer them: edge cases (NaN, ±infinity, -0.0, zero and ±1, non-ASCII text, empty and up to 16× bigger inputs) and shrunk inputs (tiny and random slices). Nothing is enabled until every case matches: same values (floats within 1e-9), errors where the original errors. A port that is right but slower per call than the original (calling into Rust costs more than the work saved) isn't enabled either. `FAST_ANYTHING_DISABLE=1` runs the original any time. ## Results Real runs on an i5-10500, Windows 11 (C and C++: a 4-core GitHub Actions Linux runner). Reproduce them from [`examples/`](examples). | app | before | after | |---|---|---| | Python fuzzy dedupe (700 names) | 4.91s | **42ms, 116×** | | TypeScript fuzzy dedupe (2,000 names) | 3.11s | **155ms, 20×** | | PHP fuzzy dedupe (600 names) | 2.94s | **53ms, 55×** | | Go fuzzy dedupe (3,000 names) | 3.02s | **144ms, 21×** | | Ruby fuzzy dedupe (400 names) | 3.13s | **228ms, 14×** | | C# fuzzy dedupe (4,000 names) | 4.03s | **312ms, 13×** | | Java fuzzy dedupe (4,000 names) | 3.50s | **1.18s, 3×** (11× on the function; the rest is JVM startup) | | C mandelbrot (8 zoom levels) | 431ms | **127ms, 3.4×** | | C++ fuzzy dedupe (6,000 names) | 3.02s | **1.09s, 2.7×** | fast-anything ports the outermost loop it can, not the tiny function called inside it, so the app crosses into Rust once instead of millions of times. Porting only the inner `levenshtein` gave 35× and 1.9×. ## Why not rewrite it all? - **Compile time**: each port is a one-function crate. Seconds, not minutes. - **Cache**: every port shares one `.fast/target`. Delete it whenever you like. - **Risk**: your code stays as it is. Rust is opt-in per function, checked against real behavior. ## Agents - **Claude Code plugin**: `/plugin marketplace add EL4CTEO/fast-anything`, then `/plugin install fast-anything@fast-anything` and `/fast-anything:fast python app.py` - **MCP server** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor…), built into the binary: `claude mcp add fast-anything -- fast-anything mcp`. 8 tools: `fast_scan`, `fast_port`, `fast_verify`, `fast_enable`, `fast_disable`, `fast_bench`, `fast_report`, `fast_status`. - **Skill**: [`skills/fast-anything`](skills/fast-anything/SKILL.md) teaches any agent the loop. ## Languages | language | binding | status | |---|---|---| | Python 3.10+ | PyO3 | ✅ | | JavaScript / TypeScript (Node 22+, Bun, Deno 2+: `bun app.ts`, `deno run -A app.ts`) | napi-rs | ✅ | | Ruby 3.3+ | C ABI + JSON, through Ruby's built-in Fiddle | ✅ | | Java 22+ (`java App.java`, Maven, Gradle) | the same C bridge, through the FFM API | ✅ | | Kotlin/JVM (Gradle, `src/main/kotlin`, JDK 22+) | the Java bridge; top-level functions, `object` and companion members, extension functions | ✅ | | Go 1.22+ (`go run .`) | the same C bridge, through the Windows loader or dlopen (cgo) | ✅ | | PHP 8.1+ (`php app.php`) | the same C bridge, through PHP's FFI extension (`extension=ffi`) | ✅ | | C and C++ (gcc, clang or Intel oneAPI icx/icpx: `clang -O2 main.c lib.c`) | the same C bridge, through LoadLibrary or dlopen | ✅ | | C# / .NET 8+ (`dotnet run -c Release`) | the same C bridge, through NativeLibrary; profiled with EventPipe, nothing to install | ✅ | It ports top-level, deterministic functions that take plain data (numbers, strings, lists, dicts, typed arrays…), including ones in your entry script when its main code sits under `if __name__ == "__main__":` (or `if __FILE__ == $0`, or `if (import.meta.main)` / `if (require.main === module)`). In Python that means module-level functions and `@staticmethod`s (dataclasses, NamedTuples and numeric NumPy arrays count as plain data), in Java, C# and PHP static methods (and PHP functions), in Go plain functions, in C and C++ free functions and static methods. `scan` says why anything else can't move yet. With Intel oneAPI on Windows, run fast-anything from a shell where `setvars.bat` ran (it sets up the linker). SYCL kernels run on the device and aren't ported; with `-fsycl`, only host functions are profiled and ported. Ruby, Java, Go, PHP, C, C++ and C# need no headers, bindings or extra tools: the port is a plain Rust library with one C entry point taking and returning JSON, and fast-anything replays the recorded calls against it directly. Any language that can call C can use that bridge. ## License MIT

# VIctory fork (work in progress)

A work-in-progress fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a
compatibility layer that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from
files the user supplies. This fork follows upstream
`main` and adds fixes aimed at one goal: getting the game's world to render
correctly and playably on one particular PC.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's
developer or publisher.

## Credits

- **[VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory)** by Marvisak and its
  contributors is the base of everything here: the loader, the runtime
  services, the Direct3D 12 back end and the shader recompiler. Licensed
  GPL-3.0-or-later; so is this fork. Upstream's history is kept intact below
  the single commit that carries this fork's changes.
- **[XCL](https://github.com/ivall/xcl)** by ivall and its contributors
  (GPL-2.0-only) was used as a reference for how the same title behaves under
  another layer. Fixes inspired by it were written anew in VIctory's code.
- This fork's changes were developed with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

## Status of this fork (2026-11-25)

**Not playable yet: 2.5 to 4 frames per second, and shadowed areas are black.**
Tested on one machine: Windows 11, Intel i7-14700KF, NVIDIA RTX 4070 12 GB,
32 GB RAM. The Series X profile is used throughout.

| Stage | State in this fork |
|-------|--------------------|
| Boot, menus, start screen | works, 30 fps (as upstream) |
| Opening cutscene | plays from start to finish, in order, lit: title cards, credits cards, night and dusk shots |
| Saves | the game autosaves a checkpoint and loads it again |
| First gameplay scene (the prologue) | renders: characters, textures, sky, sunlit exterior; HUD, pause menu and pad input work |
| Light in shadow | missing: the game's ray-traced bounce light and ray-traced lamp and sun shadows do not run yet, so anything the sun does not hit directly is black |
| Frame rate in the world | 2-4 fps: 420-450 ms per frame by default, 240-350 ms with the newer switches (`VICTORY_RELAY=2`, or `VICTORY_LATE_WAIT=3 VICTORY_WIDE_BACK=1 VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MIN_MB=1 VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MB=1024`); it started at 3-6 seconds per frame |
| Stability | no driver hang or device loss in normal runs (a hang introduced by the wave64 update was found and fixed: its barrier form for 64-lane programs is now off unless `VICTORY_WAVE_WIDE=1`) |

### What this fork changed (summary)

Rendering:
- Meshlet culling read its scene buffers as the wrong kind of view, so the world drew almost nothing; fixed.
- Per-draw descriptor tables could run out, after which draws used slots never made for them and the card hung; fixed.
- Light packed by the game's compute shaders was read back through empty copies (sky, probes, fog); fixed for every mip level and layer.
- The fog reconstruction, shadow-mask, hair, blend-shape skinning, fire and several material programs did not translate; fixed.
- Gathers at a named mip level (with and without an offset) read level 0; fixed.
- Implicit-level samples outside pixel shaders produced invalid DXIL in 730 compute programs; fixed.
- Rectangle lists, depth and stencil twins for depth textures written by compute, texture read-backs.
- Ray tracing, in progress and off by default: the game's own structure-builder programs translate, title memory can be read by raw address from shaders, the hardware ray/box and ray/triangle test is emulated in DXIL (checked against a reference on the GPU), and 59 of the 64 trace programs translate. Nothing is lit by it yet. See [docs/fork-ray-tracing.md](docs/fork-ray-tracing.md).

Speed and memory:
- Waits for memory values, write-watch queries and page queries no longer walk page tables per call.
- Large title buffers get a copy in card memory, with shader writes found by hashing on the card.
- Submissions can be sent ahead of the wait for the card (`VICTORY_LATE_WAIT`), with a relay thread that lands results as the card finishes (`VICTORY_RELAY`): in a first five-minute run the card's idle time behind the submitting thread fell from about 136 to 30 ms per frame.
- Title memory can be opened as a graphics heap so that buffers are used in place instead of copied (`VICTORY_INPLACE`, first stage only; a probe confirmed the approach on the test GPU).
- The bindless texture queue no longer uploads stale views; the view table no longer grows without bound; the pipeline library is mapped instead of read into memory.
- An intermittent device loss was traced to the pipeline library file being replaced while mapped; fixed.

- Translated shaders get clean-up passes over the finished module (dead code, constant folding, reuse of values, branch facts); the pack's host instruction count falls by about 43 %, worth about 20 ms of GPU time per frame on the test machine (`VICTORY_SHADER_OPT=0` turns them off).

Most of the newer speed changes sit behind environment switches that are off
by default (`VICTORY_LATE_WAIT`, `VICTORY_RELAY`, `VICTORY_WIDE_BACK`,
`VICTORY_CARD_BUFFERS_MIN_MB`, `VICTORY_INPLACE`, `VICTORY_BVH_BUILDER`, ...).
Each is described in a comment where it is read.

### Known problems

- Everything in shadow is black (see above).
- The interior of the first gameplay room is sometimes not drawn after the cutscene hands over to gameplay.
- Around 24 GB of memory is in use during play.
- A few style lints are switched off for this fork in the workspace `Cargo.toml` until the newer code is tidied.
- Many changes here are specific to this title and this GPU, and some are marked `shortcut:` in the code where they approximate what the console does.

Everything below this line is upstream VIctory's own README, unchanged; its
status section describes upstream, not this fork.

|-------|-------|
| Boot, first-boot screens (accessibility, language, settings, legal) | works, 30 fps |
| Intro video with sound | works |
| Start screen, profile and saves | works |

| Subsystem | Today | Needs |
|-----------|-------|-------|

| Input | XInput pads, keyboard, keyboard stand-in pad | Trigger rumble |

Input: XInput pads. With none connected the keyboard is a pad while the
title's window has focus:

| Keys | Pad |
|------|-----|
| W A S D / I J K L | left / right stick |
| arrows | D-pad |
| Enter, Backspace, X, Y | A, B, X, Y |
| Q / E, Z / C | shoulders, triggers |

```

victory shader-info [paths...] [--verbose] [--disasm]
```

## Debugging

A release build has no debugging aids. Build them in with

```powershell
cargo build --profile diag -p victory --features diagnostics   # target\diag\victory.exe
```

| Variable | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `VICTORY_LOG=<target>=debug,...` | debug and trace output |
| `VICTORY_STACKS=20,60` | every thread's stack at those seconds |
| `VICTORY_WATCH=<rva>,...` | logs a title u32 when it changes |

# VIctory fork for AMD Radeon (work in progress)

This is a fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory) by Marvisak
and its contributors. It follows upstream `main` up to `8e79c80` (2026-11-24),
carries a number of upstream pull requests, and adds fixes found while running
the game's world on one AMD card.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's
developer or publisher.

## State of this fork (2026-11-25)

**Not playable yet: 5 to 7 frames per second.** Tested on one machine only:
Windows 11, AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB, Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 64 GB RAM, Series X
profile. Nothing here has been run on an NVIDIA or Intel card.

| What | State on that machine |
|------|-----------------------|
| Boot, menus | work, 30 fps (as upstream) |
| The world | renders lit, with textures, people, vehicles, vegetation, water and sky |
| Saves | load and store |
| Frame rate in the world | 5 to 8 fps (7.2 to 7.7 standing still in a scene of 8,800 draws; less while driving). Shown in the picture's top left corner (`VICTORY_FPS=0` hides it) |
| Light in shadow | a stand-in that follows the game's sky by day and by night, less of it in creases and under objects: the game's ray-traced indirect light does not run |
| Reflections | the game's, held down: without rays every glossy surface reflected the open sky, indoors too, and floors looked whitewashed |
| Shadows of the sun and of lamps | the game's own, and they work; too much of the constant light drowns them |
| Distant trees | drawn |
| Vehicles in motion | whole (they lost and stretched parts until the copies of title memory saw writes through every view of a page) |
| In-game phone | **broken**: with the phone out the world is unlit (black) and the phone is an empty outline |
| Memory | about 22 GB of RAM and more video memory than a 16 GB card has |

A driver timeout (Windows resets the display driver, every monitor goes black
for a moment) happened once in the session this was written in. Expect it.

### What this fork changes over upstream

Picture:
- The world's indirect diffuse light is replaced by a constant while the ray
  passes do not run. What the game's resolve pass left instead was bright
  magenta on leaves, cloth and paper, and blocks of colours indoors
  (`VICTORY_AMBIENT=<level>`, 0.6 by default; `off` keeps the game's output).
  Its colour can be set (`VICTORY_AMBIENT_TINT=r,g,b`), and less of it
  reaches creases, corners and the underside of things, worked out from the
  scene's depth alone (`VICTORY_AMBIENT_SHADE=strength,radius`; grainy, it is
  not blurred yet). In diagnostics builds all of it can be tuned in a running
  game from a file (`VICTORY_AMBIENT_FILE`). It follows the sky dome the
  game draws for its reflections (`VICTORY_AMBIENT_SKY=off` keeps the
  constant, `gain,least,power` sets it): its level is `gain * mean^power +
  least` with the sky's hue, so night, dawn and noon need no hand-set level.
- Translated shaders get clean-up passes before they are written (dead
  code, constants, one instruction for one value, branch facts, one read
  for one place), taken from the VIctory fork at commit ba8697aa and
  adapted (`VICTORY_SHADER_OPT=0` turns them off). All 25,623 shaders this
  fork emits for the game pass Microsoft's validator with them. The first
  launch after such a change rebuilds every pipeline (minutes of black
  world) and **the water is missing until the game is started again**.
- The game's reflections are held to a part of that constant light after
  its last reflection pass (`VICTORY_AMBIENT_REFLECT`, 0.5 by default, 0
  leaves them alone). Without rays they are the sky's, unoccluded.
- Blending is off on integer render targets in host pipelines: the console
  ignores it there, D3D12 refuses the pipeline. One world pipeline the driver
  refused at every launch is made now (pull request #45, pgm1207 and Arvi23).
- In pixel shaders every read of another pixel of the same 2x2 quad goes
  through quad reads, helper pixels included. Wave reads return 0 from helper
  pixels on AMD, which showed as lines along every triangle on car paint,
  glass and skin. Upstream does this after discards only.
- A helper pixel's `v_readfirstlane` reads its own value (upstream `0601955`).
- Twice the dynamic descriptor slots, so the tables of heavy frames fit.
- Depth and stencil twins for depth textures written by compute, screen
  passes with pipeline workers of their own, textures told apart by the mips
  their memory really holds, and other fixes listed in the history.

Speed:
- The clamps of a run of indirect draws are recorded in a list before the
  list that draws, and run one after another (`VICTORY_HOIST_CLAMPS`, 7 by
  default, 0 for each before its draw): 225 to about 80 ms of GPU time per
  frame in a scene of 9,000 draws.
- The snapshots and the copy-back of the tiles shaders write are taken on
  several threads (pull request #18, PikPakPik): copying back went from
  about 43 to about 33 ms a frame here. The frame rate did not move.
- The title's submissions return before the host GPU is done, with what
  they owe finished at the next wait (`VICTORY_ASYNC_SUBMIT=0` turns it
  off): 200-238 to 150-186 ms a frame in the same place. It gained nothing
  until the next two changes were in.
- Title memory the game shows one 64 KiB view at a time is used in place:
  its pages follow one another in their section, so the stretch is mapped
  once more at an address of ours and the host heap opened there
  (`VICTORY_STRETCH=0` turns it off). Copying back went from 36 to 12 ms a
  frame. Ranges made of several stretches are still copied.
- The table of descriptor views is a read-write lock. A PIX timing capture
  showed the game's five recording threads taking turns on it as a mutex,
  6,600 context switches a second each.
- Thin LTO and one codegen unit for the release profile (pull request #96,
  Key-rs), and eight changes by romainhedouin that take repeated work out
  of the draw path (#24, #25, #27, #28, #29, #30, #33, #34). None of the
  eight moved the frame time measurably here; nothing broke.
- What a frame still waits for, from the same capture: the thread that
  submits, which prepares each batch while the host GPU is idle (the plan
  of directly indexed descriptors walks every slot, `bindless_plan`), and
  copies of title memory, about 100 MB a frame.
- Shader cache entries of another build can be reused
  (`VICTORY_SHADER_BUILD_OF=<executable>`, diagnostics).

Memory the title shows at several addresses:
- Every view of a guarded physical page is guarded with it, so a write of
  the title's through another address is seen (the idea of victory-fork
  #115 and victory-amd, written anew here); blocks the kernel is about to
  write stay writable for two seconds. Before this, parts of moving
  vehicles were left behind; the distant trees' quads that crossed the
  screen have not come back since either (cause not proven).

AMD:
- Shaders that crash or never leave the AMD driver's compiler cost only
  their pipeline, not the run.
- Buffer element counts come from the host's own table, not a size query the
  driver's compiler crashes on.

Lifetimes: a list keeps the copies of title memory whose addresses it gives
as root views, and objects the title let go of are kept eight seconds at
least (32 presented frames were a third of a second in the menus).

Diagnostics: every translated shader is logged with its DXIL hash, the one
[Radeon GPU Detective](https://gpuopen.com/radeon-gpu-detective/) names a
shader in flight by, so its crash reports can be matched to the game's
programs. Diagnostics builds: `VICTORY_SHADER_PATCH` changes one word of a
shader's machine code before translation, `VICTORY_SHADER_SWAP` replaces
shader containers by files, `VICTORY_ALWAYS_COPY=1` refreshes every copy of
title memory each frame, `VICTORY_GPU_TIMING=1` logs GPU time per pipeline.
Each is described in a comment where it is read.

### How it is run here

A diagnostics build (`cargo build --profile diag -p victory --features
diagnostics`), with:

```
VICTORY_PRESENT_TARGET=1x1:1
VICTORY_HAIR=1
victory run <game_scarlett_master.exe> --execute --console series-x
```

The first launch after a build translates every shader and builds about
2,500 pipelines; the loading screen can stay frozen, with sound, for minutes.

### Known problems

- With the in-game phone out the world is unlit (see the table).
- The per-draw descriptor slots are few for the heaviest places: when they
  run out, some draws of a frame are dropped.
- Memory: the process commits about 33 GB after a quarter of an hour's
  drive (the title's own 7 GB, 8 GB of textures on the card, copies of its
  buffers, and the system's backing of video memory).
- No ray-traced light; what stands in for it is the same everywhere in a
  frame. With the sky following turned off the constant of 0.6 is too much at
  night and too little at noon.
- Streamed textures are capped at 1024 pixels a side (512, then 256, as
  video memory fills): at 2048 this 16 GB card goes 1 to 2 GB over its
  budget (`VICTORY_TEXTURE_MAX=2048` to try).
- Some compute programs do not translate (ray-tracing structure builders,
  wind volumes, a few others) and their passes are dropped. With
  `VICTORY_RAYS=1` the builders translate and run, and the device is
  removed a minute and a half later: do not expect light from it. Two
  causes found with AMD's Radeon GPU Detective are fixed (lists and
  descriptors named copies of title memory that were already destroyed);
  the run now ends on a read at an address no resource ever had.
- Some draws of a frame are dropped in the world for want of a host
  pipeline: 266 programs of the pack do not translate (195 take console
  addresses in scalar registers: the ray-tracing builders and a family of
  geometry shaders; 71 mesh shaders pass the host's 32 KiB of outputs), and
  the AMD driver's compiler crashes on one compute program. Four mesh
  pipelines counted as refused before were only on the list of pipelines
  the driver's compiler does not end, put there by a rule that fired while
  the world loads; delete `pipelines/crashed.txt` in the cache folder if
  an older build wrote it. The program that activates the screen probes'
  rays is left out on purpose while rays do not run.
- Windows 10 is reported not to get past start-up without a newer D3D12
  runtime (issue #9, pull request #44, not merged or tried here yet); this
  fork has only been run on Windows 11.
- Tests that fail on this machine, before and after this update:
  `list::tests::lists_are_cut_at_waits_that_follow_work` in `victory-gpu`
  and five `xmem` tests in `victory-hle` (issues #2 and #8).
- `crates/victory-shader/src/emit/lower.rs` is larger than the size limit of
  `cargo xtask policy`; it is source code, not an asset.
- Many changes are specific to this title and this GPU, and some are marked
  `shortcut:` in the code where they approximate what the console does.

### Credits

- **[VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory)** by Marvisak and its
  contributors is the base of everything here. Licensed GPL-3.0-or-later; so
  is this fork. Upstream's history and the authors of the pull requests
  carried here are kept in the commit history.
- Pull requests merged into this fork, read line by line and run in the
  world before merging: #45 (pgm1207, sent by Arvi23), #18 (PikPakPik),
  #96 (Key-rs), and #24, #25, #27, #28, #29, #30, #33, #34 (romainhedouin).
  About ninety others are still to be read, the larger speed changes
  first; thank you for them, for the test reports, and for the advice to
  take a PIX timing capture, which found more in an hour than a day of
  our own counters.
- [fxceless/victory-fork](https://github.com/fxceless/victory-fork) and
  [myokex/victory-amd](https://github.com/myokex/victory-amd) were read for
  comparison; no code of theirs is in this fork.
- [XCL](https://github.com/ivall/xcl) by ivall: its README was read; no code
  of it is here.
- This fork's changes were developed with
  [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) and Gemini (Antigravity).

---

## From upstream's README

What follows is taken from upstream VIctory's own README: what the project
is, how to build it, its commands and its debugging switches. They apply to
this fork too. Upstream's status section is left out, because it describes
upstream's state and upstream's test machine (an RX 6700 XT), not this fork
or the machine above: read it
[in upstream's repository](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory#readme).

# VIctory

Runs Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series X|S) natively on Windows, from files
the user supplies.

The title's x86-64 code runs unchanged inside our process; VIctory supplies
the platform underneath it and converts the title's data, ahead of time where
it can and on first use where it must (shaders). See
[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

over HID as well and plays as the first pad when no XInput pad answers. With
no pad connected the keyboard is a pad while the title's window has focus:

| Keys | Pad |
|------|-----|
| W A S D / I J K L | left / right stick |
| arrows | D-pad |
| Enter, O | A, B |
| Backspace, X, Y | B, X, Y |
| Q / E, Z / C | shoulders, triggers |
| F / H | stick clicks |

```

victory shader-info [paths...] [--verbose] [--disasm]

            [--console series-x|series-s] [-- <title arguments>]
```

## Debugging

A release build has no debugging aids. Build them in with


| `VICTORY_CRASH_SAVE=<rva>:<len>,...` | saves title memory to the cache folder on a crash |
| `VICTORY_CAPTURE=<dir>` | saves presented frames (powers of two, or `VICTORY_CAPTURE_FRAMES=<list>`) |
| `VICTORY_DUMP_TARGETS=1` | with the two above, saves every render target of those frames |

| `VICTORY_D3D12_GBV=1` | with the above, GPU-based validation (bad descriptor use reported, not faulted; slow) |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_DRED=1` | on a GPU failure, the allocation hit and the commands in flight |
| `VICTORY_SKIP_PIPELINES=<hash>,...` | omit draws and dispatches, including indirect ones, whose pipeline contains a listed 16-digit shader hash |

items.readme:
Leonida Continued

Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy.

Other languages | Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Discord | Telegram

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. > Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes > from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. > [!NOTE] > **This is a continuation of [NotRexed's Leonida project](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida).** The original > author has left the project, and development continues here with its full commit history. Credit for the work up to > that point belongs to NotRexed and the contributors listed in the history. Discord: https://discord.gg/ETf4qj5acN Telegram: https://t.me/mandyport Original author's Git Mirror: https://git.notrexed.dev/notrexed/Leonida
## Project status **Early. It's built on your PC from your own copy. **The easy way:** 1. Install the prerequisites below. 2. Download this project **with its submodule**: `git clone --recursive https://github.com/ubiquitarianism/leonida`. A "Download ZIP" from GitHub leaves out `third_party/rpf9-explorer`. The build fetches it if `git` is installed, and otherwise tells you what to do. 3. Double-click **`Build.bat`**. On Linux or macOS, run **`./Build.sh`** from a terminal instead (see [docs/linux.md](docs/linux.md) for Linux). It finds your copy of the game by itself: it looks in Downloads, Desktop, Documents (also where Windows keeps them, such as in OneDrive), Games, your home folder and the top of every drive, two folders deep. It recognises the version from a few file sizes, without reading anything large. If you have more than one copy it asks which one, and if it finds none it asks you to paste the folder. Before starting it checks that everything below is installed and that there is enough free space, and it lists anything missing in one go. The result goes to `Documents\Leonida`. A stopped build continues where it left off. Your game folder is the one that holds `MicrosoftGame.Config` and the `.rpf` archives, as plain files. **Prerequisites:** - **Your own copy** of the Xbox Series package, version 1.0.2.1. - **Windows 10/11 x64**, with about **400 GB** free for work files (an assets export alone measured about 337 GB before its audio step, in about 2 h 35 min). Disk sizes here are as Windows Explorer shows them, which are GiB: 400 GiB is about 430 GB in decimal units. They can go on another drive with `--work`. - [Python 3.12+](https://www.python.org/downloads/) (tick "Add python.exe to PATH"). - [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0). - [Vulkan SDK](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/), for `spirv-as` / `spirv-val`. - [LLVM 21+](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/releases) with the **AMDGPU target** for `llvm-mc`. The official Windows build has no AMDGPU target. On Windows, `scripts\build_llvm_mc.ps1` builds a native `llvm-mc.exe` with it (no WSL; needs git and the Visual Studio C++ tools below) and sets `LLVM_MC`; it takes about 20-40 minutes. A faster way, if you use [conda](https://docs.conda.io/): `conda install -c conda-forge llvm-tools` (its Windows build includes the AMDGPU target; [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md) used version 23.1.6), then set `LLVM_MC` to the full path of the `llvm-mc.exe` it installs (`where.exe llvm-mc` shows it once the environment is active; in PowerShell a bare `where` is `Where-Object`). Or install `llvm-21` in WSL and set `LLVM_MC` to the whole command, `LLVM_MC="wsl -d Ubuntu -e /usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc"` (see [docs/design.md](docs/design.md#disassembling-shaders)). On Linux, `llvm-mc` on PATH is enough, and so is a versioned distribution install such as Ubuntu's `llvm-21` (`llvm-mc-21`, `/usr/lib/llvm-21/bin/llvm-mc`). - Visual Studio 2022 with **Desktop development with C++** and the **Windows SDK 10.0.26100 or newer**, for the runtime stage (the runtime uses version 1.2 root signatures, which older SDKs don't declare). - [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) on PATH (optional: decodes the XMA2 streams, and required for `--wav`). **Is this PC strong enough?** [Can I Run Leonida](https://assttro.github.io/can-i-run-leonida/) is a lightweight browser-based checker that compares your PC against reference profiles. It's a rough estimate, not a benchmark. **Low disk space:** the ~400 GB figure is for the full build. To *run* the port, `--stages check,shaders,runtime` needs about 30 GB; the `assets` stage (~370 GB) is only for the asset tools, and `--wav` adds several times the Ogg Opus size (the preflight prints this choice when the assets stage is what does not fit). `--work` and `--out` can sit on another drive. The runtime maps the package in place, so a read-only package drive needs `gta6rt --overlay `; `--overlay` is a `gta6rt` option, not a `make_game.py` one. Leave the `.s` files in `work/shaders/dxbc/disasm` in place: the next run checks them against the list in `disasm.done` and disassembles the missing ones again (all of them for a folder whose `disasm.done` predates that list), then translates every shader again. A `disasm` folder that is a symlink is refused when the stage has to clear it. **Disk space and drives:** the build uses three folders, and each can be on its own drive: | Folder | Flag | What is in it | Size | Read when playing | |---|---|---|---|---| | your package | `--game` | your copy of the game; only read, never written | as copied | yes, in place (`game_path.txt`) | | work | `--work` (default `\work`) | `shaders` (carved, disassembled, translated) and `assets` (exports) | about 30 GB + about 370 GB | only `shaders\spirv` (`shader_path.txt`) | | port | `--out` (default `Documents\Leonida`) | `gta6rt.exe`, its DLL, the path files, the pipeline cache, `overlay` | small | yes | The free-space check before a build counts the `--work` drive only, because that is where the large files go. Nothing in `\assets` is read by the game, so with a small SSD you can keep what the game loads on the SSD and put the exports on a hard drive, in two runs: ```powershell # on the SSD: the package, the port and the translated shaders (about 30 GB of work files) python -I make_game.py --game "S:\Games\package" --out "S:\Games\Leonida" --work "S:\Games\Leonida\work" --stages check,shaders,runtime,pipelines # on the hard drive: the asset exports (about 370 GB), only for the asset tools python -I make_game.py --game "S:\Games\package" --out "S:\Games\Leonida" --work "H:\leonida-assets" --stages check,assets ``` The second run does not rebuild the runtime, so `shader_path.txt` keeps pointing at the SSD. Pass the same `--work` again for later runs of each stage so they resume. A single `--work "H:\leonida-work"` also works; the game then loads its translated shaders from that drive. **From a terminal**, with the same behaviour and more control: ```powershell python -I make_game.py --find # list the copies found on this PC python -I make_game.py --pick # choose the game folder in a folder dialog python -I make_game.py --check # check your copy, build nothing python -I make_game.py --check --full-check # also compare SHA-256 of every file (slow) python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --out "D:\Games\Leonida" --work "E:\leonida-work" python -I make_game.py --stages shaders,assets # only some stages python -I make_game.py --game "D:\path\to\your\package" --wav # also decode Opus to PCM WAV (large) python -I make_game.py --wave64-emulate off # auto (default), on or off; see below ``` `--wave64-emulate` decides whether wave64 compute and mesh shaders are translated to be exact on any subgroup size (see "Wave64 emulation" in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)). NVIDIA and Intel GPUs have 32-wide subgroups and need it. The default, `auto`, asks `vulkaninfo` (part of the Vulkan SDK) and turns emulation on if any GPU lacks 64-wide subgroups or its subgroup size is unknown. It also checks whether the runtime's GPU can run compute and mesh shaders 64-wide. With `--mesh-compute`, only compute subgroup support is needed. On AMD's Windows driver, `auto` uses native wave64 on RDNA1 and RDNA2 when the runtime's GPU supports it, even if another GPU is 32-wide or `vulkaninfo` is unavailable. That driver can crash on emulated LDS code (#857). For RDNA1 cards without mesh support, the decision uses the compute stage, which can run wave64 without native mesh support. The mode is saved next to the translated shaders, and changing it translates them again. `auto` can normally reuse previously emulated shaders. The AMD Windows workaround rebuilds those shaders in native mode. Use `--wave64-emulate on` to force emulation or `--wave64-emulate off` to force native wave64. Four fallback flags are forwarded to the translator the same way, saved next to the translated shaders, and changing them translates them again: `--no-float-controls` (drop `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve`, for devices whose pipeline check skips a shader without `shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32`; needs PR #664's translator flag), `--bary-fallback` (read raw barycentrics from an interpolated input, for devices without `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric`), `--texel-offset-fallback` (fold `image_sample*_o` offsets into the coordinate, for devices without `VK_KHR_maintenance8`) and `--mesh-compute` (mesh shaders as compute, for devices without `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`; on by itself on Intel's Windows Vulkan driver, whose native mesh draws crash, BUILD-2202, unless `--native-mesh`). Each is documented in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). The build records which llvm-mc command and version produced the disassembly. Changing either, or reusing a work folder that predates this record, reruns disassembly and translation while keeping the extracted shader inputs. The build records which translator sources produced the shaders. A change to those files reruns translation using the saved disassembly. Older work folders need one translation after upgrading to record this information. The build also records which decoder (the `third_party/rpf9-explorer` commit and the `tools/rpf9dump` sources) exported each archive's models and textures and each texture pool. When it changes, the assets stage removes that export and makes it again. Older work folders have no record, so their models, textures and pools are exported once more after upgrading. Stages: `check` always runs first; then `shaders`, `assets` and `runtime` run together when selected (they do not depend on each other). `pipelines` starts once the translated shaders are ready and, when this run includes runtime, that stage has finished rebuilding `vk_pipeline_check`, so it can overlap the rest of assets; it creates every translated shader on your GPU driver, reports any it has to skip, and saves a pipeline cache to `pipeline_cache.bin` in `--out` (the runtime doesn't load that cache yet, so it doesn't speed up the first boot). The shader translation is the longest CPU step: it runs on `--jobs` processes (half the CPU threads by default). When shaders and assets share the machine, that budget is split between them and passed to `rpf9dump` as `--jobs`; a solo assets run still lets `rpf9dump` use every core. Progress lines include percent and a rough ETA for translation shards, asset steps, and overall stage completion. On an interactive terminal, a LEONIDA setup screen lets you set jobs and whether stages overlap, then a key-switchable per-stage log view (`1`–`4` / `Tab`) keeps parallel output demuxed; full stage logs go under `work/logs/`. Use `--no-tui` (or redirect stdout) for the plain console. `--wav` is off by default because 16-bit PCM WAV is several times larger than Ogg Opus. It decodes the repackaged Ogg Opus streams to `work\assets\audio\wav` after the audio bank step; existing WAV files are skipped when a build resumes. ### Vulkan diagnostics on Linux With CMake 3.24+, a C++20 compiler, and Vulkan development headers and loader installed: ```sh cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build/linux cmake --build runtime/build/linux --parallel ./runtime/build/linux/vk_pipeline_check /path/to/spirv ``` Pass the directory containing `index.json` and the translated SPIR-V files to `vk_pipeline_check`. `make_game.py` runs on Linux too. The `pipelines` stage uses the `vk_pipeline_check` built above (`runtime/build/linux`, or `runtime/build`), and builds it there itself before any other work if it is missing. ### Running the loader on Linux The loader is a Windows program and runs under Wine or Proton; CI runs its tests under Wine on every push to `main` that changes `runtime/`, and on demand from the Actions tab (the `wine` job of the Runtime workflow). On Linux the `runtime` stage cross-builds it into `runtime/build/windows` with clang-cl and lld-link (LLVM 19+, but not 22.1.7 or 22.1.8, see [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#known-problems); plain names, or all five LLVM tools with one version suffix such as `clang-cl-21`) against the MSVC CRT and Windows SDK that [xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin) lays out, in `XWIN_DIR` or `~/.local/share/xwin-sdk` ([docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md#the-windows-runtime-on-linux-under-wine-or-proton) has the one-time `xwin` command). Without them the stage is left out of the default stages, and asking for it lists what is missing before any work starts. A Windows build made elsewhere works too, such as the `runtime-windows` artifact of that workflow's `windows` job, unzipped: ```sh python3 -I make_game.py --runtime-build ~/Downloads/runtime-windows ``` Either way it copies `gta6rt.exe` and `gta6rt_tls_host.dll` into `--out` and writes `gta6rt.sh` next to them, which starts `gta6rt.exe` with `wine`, or with the Wine named by `WINE` (for Proton, its `files/bin/wine`). The same option skips the build on Windows. On Linux, run `/gta6rt.sh --dry-run` to inspect the packaged title's imports, then `/gta6rt.sh --init` to check TLS callbacks and DLL initialization. Use `/gta6rt.sh --run` for startup. These commands use the package in `game_path.txt`, the port's `overlay` for writes, and Vulkan by default. When the Vulkan backend is selected with `LEONIDA_D3D12=vulkan`, the packaged runtime finds the translated shaders in `/shaders/spirv` using `shader_path.txt` beside `gta6rt.exe`. Set `LEONIDA_SHADERS` to use another directory. ## How it works | Piece | What it does | Where | |---|---|---| | Version check | Every package file's name, size and SHA-256 for each supported version | `game/`, `make_game.py` | | Shader pipeline | Carves DXBC containers from `shaders.rpf` without its encrypted table of contents. Unpacks the `XBCH` → `FSSM` native RDNA2 program, disassembles it with LLVM (`gfx1013`) and translates it to SPIR-V | `tools/shader_carve.py` ([optional Rust scanner](tools/shader_carve_native/README.md)), `fssm_unpack.py`, `shader_disasm.py`, `rdna2spirv.py` | | Asset export | Finds validated resources inside RPF9 archives and the loose `.ttpf` texture pools | `tools/rpf9dump` (on rpf9-explorer's Core) | | Runtime | Maps the PE image, resolves imports to shims (GDK, XMem, `d3d12_xs`) | `runtime/` | | Research tools | PE/RTTI inspection, raw carving, texture tiling probes, GPU test harnesses | `tools/`, `runtime/test/` | | Progress dashboard | One offline page of what passes, what changed since it last passed and what blocks next, built from test results and the docs' own tables; nothing is written inside the repo | `tools/progress_dashboard.py` | Localized string tables are decoded by `tools/text_tables.py` ([docs/text.md](docs/text.md)); their language is guessed from script (kana, hangul, CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic) or Latin words, and subtitles are joined to dialogue lines across languages. The translator's runtime contract (user SGPRs, push constants, memory model, bindless images, vertex fetch, system values) and all the format notes are in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md); the format, asset, runtime and validation notes are indexed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). The Xbox D3D12 plan is in [docs/d3d12_vulkan.md](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md). Audio bank formats and the export tools are in [docs/audio.md](docs/audio.md); [docs/related_projects.md](docs/related_projects.md) records the prior art we may read and the licence limits on it. ## Want to help? The biggest open pieces: - **Shader translator on hardware**: compute, mesh and geometry now translate (see the translator contract in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md)); still open are the vertex-shader input layout (`v0` = `VertexIndex` is unverified if the console runs VS as NGG) and wave64 cross-half code in VS/PS/GS on 32-wide subgroups. - **Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan**: mesh-shader draws, indirect draw state and stream output are still open; #313 tracks the remaining method surface, and nothing has been checked against the real executable yet ([plan and status](docs/d3d12_vulkan.md)). - **Model recovery**: investigate the 71 unrecovered fragment candidates in [`levels.rpf`](docs/models.md#full-archive-re-count-at-e293917). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). items.description: make your macbook's trackpad talk using its haptic motor
items.readme:
```text
────────────────────────  a90.com presents  ─────────────────────────

    _   __ ____      _____  ____   ______ ___     __ __  ______ ____
   / | / // __ \    / ___/ / __ \ / ____//   |   / //_/ / ____// __ \
  /  |/ // / / /    \__ \ / /_/ // __/  / /| |  / ,<   / __/  / /_/ /
 / /|  // /_/ /    ___/ // ____// /___ / ___ | / /| | / /___ / _, _/
/_/ |_/ \____/    /____//_/    /_____//_/  |_|/_/ |_|/_____//_/ |_|

─  haptic voice synthesis  ─────────────────────────────  trackpad  ─
```

**Mute your Mac. Your trackpad will still talk.**

There's no speaker in a MacBook trackpad, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click.
NO SPEAKER drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make sound you can hear, and turns it
into a voice. It talks, sings, raps, and becomes an instrument under your finger.

One command. About a minute and a half. No speakers used.

<!-- demo video: drag an .mp4 here in GitHub's editor -->

## 01 / before you start

```text
[ mute your mac ]        it still talks; that's the point
[ put it on a table ]    on your lap it's much quieter
[ hands off the glass ]  until it asks you to touch it
```

**Space** skips a part. **q** or **Ctrl-C** goes to the end.

## 02 / run it

`[ one line ]`

```sh
curl -fsSL a90.com/nospeaker | sh
```

Downloads the latest release to `~/.local/bin/nospeaker` and starts the show. `a90.com/nospeaker` points
to [play.sh](play.sh) in this repo, so you can read what it runs first.

`[ download ]`

Grab `nospeaker.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/os6/nospeaker/releases/latest),
unzip it and run `./nospeaker` in Terminal. Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

`[ from source ]`

Needs Xcode or the Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`). Builds one program for Apple Silicon
and Intel Macs.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/os6/nospeaker
cd nospeaker
./build.sh
./nospeaker
```

## 03 / play with it

```text
./nospeaker "hello there"            say anything
./nospeaker --voice Daniel "hello"   in another macOS voice
./nospeaker --sweep                  a rising tone, 100 Hz to 4 kHz

--dark                               white on black
--plain                              no visuals, plain text
```

## 04 / needs

A Force Touch trackpad (built into MacBooks from 2015 on, or a Magic Trackpad 2 or newer), and macOS 12 or
later on Apple Silicon, or macOS 13 or later on Intel. Without a Force Touch trackpad, it says so and exits.

```text
tested on

MacBook Pro (Mac17,10)   M5 Max   macOS 27.2.1   everything works
```

Not tested yet: Intel Macs, a Magic Trackpad, and older versions of macOS. MultitouchSupport is private, so
older systems may lack the functions it uses, and loudness differs between trackpads. If you try it on another
Mac, open an issue with your model, your macOS version and how it sounded.

## 05 / how it works

```text
say ──▶ formants ──▶ two tones ──▶ motor ──▶ glass
        per 10 ms    F1 + F2       haptics   sound
```

**Why you can hear it.** The trackpad has no speaker, but the motor moves the glass. Driven back and forth
hundreds or thousands of times a second, the glass vibrates fast enough to make sound you can hear. It's quiet
because the motor is built for short taps, not for sound.

**The motor.** `MultitouchSupport` is the private framework macOS uses for the trackpad. Its function
`MTActuationCreateFromDictionary` takes a description of a vibration, a list of sine tones with a frequency,
a strength and a length each, and `MTActuationActuate` plays it on the motor. Apple's public haptics API only
offers three fixed taps.

**The range.** Measured with the MacBook's own microphone, every semitone from 98 Hz to 3,951 Hz: how loud it
is over a quiet room, and how much of the sound is the note itself.

```text
│                                      ###
│                          #+#     +++#####        #
│                         +#+#+   .+++#####       .#
│              .       ++++#+#+   .+++#####    # #.# #
│   ++        +. . #..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+ #####.###          .#
│   +++#.     +...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+ #####.####+        .#
│  ++++#...   +...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+        .#
│ .++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+  +#    .#
│..++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+#.+#  .#.#
│..++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+#.+#+..#.#
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      131         262         523         1047        2093    3951
   public notes stop at 600 Hz ─┘

across: every semitone, in Hz · up: loudness, +16 to +34 dB
# clean note   + fair   . mostly buzz
```

It's loud from about 100 Hz to 4 kHz, with a few dead spots where the glass resonates. Its loudest, cleanest
notes are around 1 kHz, which covers the most important part of a voice.

**The voice.** macOS's own voice speaks the line into memory. Every 10 ms, linear prediction finds the voice's
two strongest resonances (formants), its loudness and its pitch. The motor plays those two resonances as tones,
restarted on every beat of the pitch, so they buzz like a voice instead of whistling. Hiss sounds (s, f, t)
become quick bursts of high tones. Two resonances beat three: in a blind test they were clearer, and louder,
because the motor's strength is split fewer ways.

It sounds robotic, and it's much easier to follow when you can read along, which is why the show types every
line as it speaks.

**The code.** One Swift file, [nospeaker.swift](nospeaker.swift), with no dependencies.

## 06 / caveats

- **Is it safe?** It never drives the motor past its normal maximum strength. Going past it is possible and
  louder, but the driver starts to stall, so nospeaker doesn't.
- MultitouchSupport is private and undocumented, so a macOS update could break this.

The MultitouchSupport function names were learned from the open-source Tactile project. Everything else was
measured on a MacBook.

```text
──────────────────────  thanks for listening  ───────────────────────
```

items.readme: # Xbox Emulator **Running the Xbox Series X|S library on PC. A continuation of [drycheetah84/TomBox](https://github.com/drycheetah84/TomBox).** The runtime reimplements the console's platform layer (Xbox-flavoured Direct3D 12, precompiled RDNA2 shaders, unified-memory textures, system libraries) so dumped, already-decrypted Xbox Series X|S builds run as normal Windows processes. It is not tied to any single title. This repo tracks our continuation — new titles brought up, platform calls extended, shader stages unlocked. Uses legally obtained, already-decrypted dumps. The runtime does no key extraction or package decryption. **Source code:** the emulator's Rust workspace is in this repo: [`crates/`](crates/), [`tools/`](tools/) and `Cargo.toml`. It contains no game files, binaries or build output. **Contributing:** pull requests are welcome, especially console library functions still marked missing in the [library map](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0. ## Status [![system functions](docs/img/badge-imports.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![Direct3D 12.x methods](docs/img/badge-d3d12x.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![RDNA2 instructions](docs/img/badge-instructions.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![shaders translated](docs/img/badge-shaders.svg)](#tested-titles) [![shader stages](docs/img/badge-stages.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![milestones](docs/img/badge-milestones.svg)](#milestones) [![titles examined](docs/img/badge-titles.svg)](#tested-titles) [![Xbox console libraries](docs/img/badge-console.svg)](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md) [![progress map](docs/img/progress.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) One square per item. The fifth section is ours and covers Xbox console libraries only: the exports of the console OS DLLs (EmbeddedXvd of every analysed title, union, so the newest console OS sets the surface) that no same-named DLL in a PC's C:\Windows\System32 exports, so console-only DLLs (d3d12_xs, xg_xs, xmem, AcpHal, chad, xapu, xcrdapi, the *legacy variants, ...) count in full and modified PC DLLs (kernel32, advapi32, mfplat, ...) only for their console-only exports, plus the GDK wrappers the emulator redirects; plain Windows DLLs (ntdll, msvcrt, ucrtbase, combase, ...) are not shown. Coloured implemented / forwarded / stub / missing; lighter squares are functions an analysed title imports. Per-title import coverage likewise counts only imports from console libraries. Generated by tools/progress/gen.py; per-function tables in docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md, headline numbers in tools/progress/summary.json. ## Milestones Counted live by `tools/progress/gen.py`; full table with evidence in [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md). | Milestone | State | |---|---| | All imported system functions covered (671/671) | done | | Full title shader sweep translated (105,506/105,506) | done | | All Direct3D 12.x methods covered | in progress (map) | | All RDNA2 instructions verified | in progress (map) | | All shader stages (Mesh, Amplification) | in progress (map) | | All Xbox console libraries covered | in progress (map) | | Fortnite boots, first frames, login, hotfix, mode select, BR lobby | done (7 run milestones) | | 3D scene correct | not reached | | Keyboard / controller input | not reached | | Audio | not reached | | Gameplay | not reached | | A second title running | not reached | ## Tested titles | Title | Build | Result | |---|---|---| | Fortnite (Chapter 2 Season 4) | 2.0.1461.7919 | Boots, logs in to a private server, reaches the lobby. 2D interface correct. 3D scene lit but the character material is wrong and bloom shows artifacts. items.description: Goal: an Xbox Series title (your own dump) on PC as the Series X version at 4K with ray tracing, picture matching the Xbox first (textures, lighting), then 30+ fps. Porting, not emulating. RX 7900 XTX first. No game files.
items.readme:
# VIctory on an RX 7900 XTX

A fork of [VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory), a compatibility layer
that runs an Xbox Series title natively on Windows from files the user supplies.
This one is about **speed on AMD RDNA 3**: the world at 30 frames a second on
one PC, without giving up the picture. It is not there yet.

**This repository contains no game files, code or assets.** You need your own
copy of the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the game's developer
or publisher.

## Where it stands (2026-11-25)

Tested on one machine only: Windows 11, Intel i9-12900K, 64 GB RAM, Radeon
RX 7900 XTX, 1440p, the Series X profile.

| | |
|---|---|
| Menus, videos, loading screens | 30 fps |
| Prologue, indoors | 50-75 ms a frame (13-20 fps) |
| First mission with the boat | 46-53 ms (19-22 fps) |
| Street chase with many cars and people | 100-165 ms (6-10 fps), single frames far longer |
| Outdoors on foot, the camp | 60-90 ms |
| Flying | 42-57 ms |
| Longest session so far | 41 minutes, no crash |
| Memory | 40-46 GB of private memory: **64 GB of RAM recommended** |

It started at 280 ms a frame in the same scenes two days earlier.

What is known to be wrong:

- Trees, plants and far buildings flicker outdoors in some places.
- Rooms with little direct light are too dark without `-RayTracing`.
- Textures of what just came into view appear late while the title streams.
- The first run with a new driver or a new build stutters while the driver makes
  pipelines (`victory warm` makes them ahead).
- Recording a frame in the world makes the title's own watchdog end it.

## How to run it

You need Windows 10/11 x64, a CPU with AVX2, a Direct3D 12 GPU with shader
model 6.6 and mesh shaders, Rust (the toolchain is pinned), the MSVC build
tools, and your own dump of the title.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/avatarmanz/VIctory-7900XTX
cd VIctory-7900XTX
copy victory.example.toml victory.toml      # then set your paths, outside this folder
cargo build --locked --profile diag -p victory --features diagnostics
scripts\play.ps1 -Exe <path of your copy's executable>
```

`scripts\play.ps1 -Safe` leaves out the newest, faster ways; try it first when
something is wrong. `-RayTracing` turns the title's ray-traced indirect light on.

Before the first run, ahead of time (both can be stopped and go on later):

```powershell
target\diag\victory.exe shaders <the shader archives>   # every shader translated, minutes
target\diag\victory.exe warm --used                     # pipelines earlier runs drew with, for a new driver or build
```

Commands, debugging switches and upstream's own description:
[docs/README-fxceless.md](docs/README-fxceless.md). Every `VICTORY_...` switch is
described in a comment where it is read.

## What is different here

In short; the reasons and the measurements are in [docs/findings.md](docs/findings.md).

- **List calls are written down, not carried out, on the title's threads**
  (`VICTORY_THIN`): eight threads of ours translate them.
- **Submissions are prepared by a thread of ours and joined**
  (`VICTORY_ASYNC_SUBMIT`, `VICTORY_JOIN_PARTS`), with what can be spread over
  threads spread: refreshes, compares (AVX2), descriptor records, landings.
- **What shaders wrote comes back beside the write guards**, by the dwords that
  changed, on a thread of its own (`VICTORY_RELAY`, `VICTORY_LAND`).
- **Buffer fills that need bytes still on the card are done on the card**
  (`VICTORY_CARD_STEPS`) instead of waiting for it.
- **The title's writes are caught more cheaply**: one view opened at a fault,
  blocks that rest, places in the title's code that look before they write.
- **Textures go up on a copy queue of their own** and a slot shows one only after
  its upload ran, which also ended a device loss that came every 15 minutes or so.
- **Boats float**: textures that shaders write and the title's CPU reads go back
  to title memory (from fxceless and Geckomacabre, on by default here).
- **Frame record and replay** with per-pass times and shader variants compared
  turn by turn ([docs/replay.md](docs/replay.md)).

## Credits

This is a tree of other people's work with more on top. The history is kept, and
commits taken from elsewhere name the commit and its author.

- **[VIctory](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory)** by Marvisak and its
  contributors: the loader, the runtime services, the Direct3D 12 back end and
  the shader recompiler.
- **[fxceless/victory-fork](https://github.com/fxceless/victory-fork)**: the fork
  this one started from, and the people whose pull requests it carries.
- **[DexNom/VIctory](https://github.com/DexNom/VIctory)**: ray tracing fixes,
  cube gradients, sparse textures.
- **[Belobug/VIctory-Belobug-AMD](https://github.com/Belobug/VIctory-Belobug-AMD)**:
  the ambient light idea, pipeline workers, and work by romainhedouin.
- **[FQY55kai/ZJOU-VICTORY](https://github.com/FQY55kai/ZJOU-VICTORY)**.
- **[myokex/victory-amd](https://github.com/myokex/victory-amd)**: the guard over
  every view of a page (with Spexivus, joroyt and tightfall), and Joshua Odom's
  reads into title memory.
- **Geckomacabre** and **cxy0072019-sketch**: the texture read-back.
- **[XCL](https://github.com/ivall/xcl)** (GPL-2.0-only) was read for how the same
  title behaves under another layer; no code of it is here.
- This fork's changes were made with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

## License

GPL-3.0-or-later, as VIctory. See [LICENSE](LICENSE); the one file that is not
covered is named in [docs/asset-policy.md](docs/asset-policy.md).
